correctness.rationale: Fourier diagonalization is proved via an elementary q-Gaussian subspace transform over every finite field. Explicit powers have the three sector formulas, checked at the boundaries t=0,1; the rank-two multiplier is strictly increasing and crosses once. The rank-one and rank-three multipliers remain negative up to that point, including the q=2 exception proved by concavity. Frequency rank counts and real double-centering give exact endpoint dimension. Exhaustive q=2,3,4 Fourier checks and high-precision root checks replay from verify.py; these corroborate, rather than replace, the proof.

value.rationale: A canonical metric on all finite-field bilinear forms has a nontrivial finite generalized roundness. The sharp exponent, the exclusive vanishing of the rank-two Fourier sector, exact endpoint Hilbert dimension, and fixed-field/fixed-dimension asymptotics are natural and useful geometric invariants. The results are not an isolated small-case value or a renaming of a previously published scalar identity.
